reviews.review:
Full Metal Schoolgirl is less a game than it is an exercise in frustration and masochism. I made it about halfway through and decided I really didn't need to see any more.

The game's main problem is that it didn't learn a critical lesson from Earth Defense Force 6, a game that came out a full three years before this (in Japan) which fixed the exact same issues this game has: weapons that took forever to reload and generally weren't fun to use. Full Metal Schoolgirl has half the weapon variety of EDF (you have four types of guns and three types of melee weapons) yet manages to have just as many weapons that no one is ever going to use.

Let me touch on the four gun types briefly, because they're a big reason why this game is bad. As previously mentioned, you have four classes of gun: snipers, shotguns, miniguns, and grenade launchers. You can only carry one gun at a time, and it's not going to be a grenade launcher because they're laughably non-viable. In practice, you're going to be carrying a shotgun or a sniper, both of which are of the "four shots then five seconds of reloading" variety. The constant reloads make the game slow to a crawl - it took me almost two and a half hours to go through roughly half of the game's 100 procedurally generated stages (from floor 1 to floor 55) using every skip the game made available to me, and most of that was due to reload times.

The reason you need the sniper or shotgun, by the way, is minibosses, which exemplify this game's enemy design. The minibosses are fat guys in suits who have a weak point on their backs but take virtually no damage from the front. They are not even remotely a threat: they're melee only and spend most of their time doing a spinning attack that will never hit you. Fighting them consists of waiting for them to do their "charge into a wall" attack which exposes their weak point for exactly long enough to get one sniper shot off. Your other option is to spend upwards of six minutes shooting at their front until their stagger bar depletes, at which point you can instantly kill them via cutscene. Said cutscene takes a good three or four seconds and you'll see it so many times that you'll get sick of it quickly.

You also need the shotgun/sniper for turrets, which are the second most annoying thing in this game. Turrets fire barrages at you which have to be guarded, which means you either spend forever keeping your shield up and firing at them for a couple of seconds or you just delete them in one hit. The rest of the enemies are just kinda there and are varying degrees of annoying to deal with but never pose an actual threat to the point where in most rooms I just stood still and killed four of them at a time with the sniper rifle before reloading for five seconds and repeating the process. 

All of this pales in comparison to the worst part of this game: the movement. The game fully expects you to platform, and the platforming SUCKS. Movement in air is extremely stiff, it's really hard to judge distance because of the camera angle, and the hitboxes on a lot of the traps are ridiculously large. The best example I can give of this is the laser traps in the first area, which will hit you seemingly at random when jumping over them even if you're well above them visually. The hitboxes on all of the traps are spaghetti and the game is FULL of them, which only slows down gameplay more as you walk through an empty hallway with sixteen electrified puddles in it or have to backtrack because a boulder or giant noh mask starts chasing you. 

I would avoid this unless you're into virtual self-flagellation or you're using it in a punishment marathon or something.

Simply said it's a dungeon crawling World Brothers with classic rogue-like all random drop on progress. Even if the playstyle might gives you difficulties, access of pre-run upgrades are accessible and adjustable for your own preferences on difficulty.

Now, let's save the cyborg labor slaves from their abusive workplace.

Fun arcade shooter with rogue-lite elements, a lot of floors to climb up but feels a bit rough on some parts. Overall it is a good experience, just maybe not for the full price without some updates regarding certain weapons and jump mechanics.

Performance wise it runs fine, but somehow doesn't give an option for 1440p resolution, while some report that 4k is an option for them (havent seen the 4k option in-game with my 1440p screens). A bit of a weird choice of only having 1080p and 4k as an option for pc, would make more sense for the consoles.

It could have used a bit more variation and the traps can be annoying at some part. I would still recommend it but be warned that it sometimes can feel a bit rough on the edges. Nothing that some updates/fine tuning cant fix.

Black void can be removed by a mod, so it shouldn't be a deal breaker for on pc.

The game is a action roguelite where you climb a 100 floor tower "freeing" employees with your firearms and chainsaw. It's fully voiced, it has some weapon variety but nothing crazy, and it is fun.
If your expecting some Binding of Issac level of synergy your not going to find it here. It's very tame and more on the level of YUKE's other titles. 

The game commits a cardinal sin for Roguelites and Likes alike. (say that ten times fast)
The runs are very long and you have to commit to them or start over. 
Not everyone has 5 hours to dedicate to a run, but you have to if you want to progress sometimes. Checkpoints are in the form of elevator keys. You receive these keys from bosses and mid-bosses and they allow you to, in a new run, continue where you met that boss, but the places get further apart as you go. starting at 10 then 35, then 55, 71, and finally 85. If your unable to make it past one of those hurtles your stuck starting at the lobby. If you only have one 85 key and die, your starting at the lobby. It gets exhausting and grindy and it wouldn't if you could save your progress mid-run. 

Also.. A lot of gooners complaining about censorship in this game make zero sense. There is an achievement for looking up her skirt, lots of anime grade sexual innuendos and the costumes exist. It's not a H-game. It was never advertised as one. Go google rule 34 ya weirdos.
